title: Training, friends and settings that make sense
summary: Keep training together, catch up with friends and talk beside shared workouts with short comments, replies and reactions. Find your preferences in focused Settings sections, keep navigating while workouts save, and see saved training changes from your other devices automatically.
changes: Open the combined reactions and comments button on a shared workout to read its inline thread. Add an optional workout reaction with a comment, reply with a tappable @name, and react to comments. Comments and replies allow up to 280 characters. Reply and comment-reaction notices appear in the notification bell. Authors can edit or delete their comments; workout owners can moderate them. Existing sharing, friendship and block rules still apply. Removed the redundant Find friends header link from Social; use the Find tab.

Settings now opens with six clear sections: Training, Appearance, Notifications, Account & privacy, Data & connections, and Help & about. Search opens the matching section and control, including profile editing. Switching sections keeps unfinished forms intact. Training groups units, goals, rest timers, workout types and bodyweight chart defaults; longer editors stay folded until needed. Export remains available for every import format.

Finish a workout or save an old session and keep navigating while the save completes. Routine notices and completion PRs no longer lock the page; failed saves retain your entries for retry and respect a screen you have moved to.

Saved workouts, bodyweight, goals and cardio refresh automatically across signed-in devices. The visible app checks every five seconds and when you return or reconnect, refreshes changed data quietly, and preserves active workouts, unsaved edits and filters. In-progress workouts stay on the device where you are logging.

Notifications and Profile now sit beside Settings in the same order on Home, Training, Social and Body. Removed the duplicate blue plus buttons from Training and Body headers; use Start for workouts and Log weigh-in for bodyweight entries.

Training combines Sessions, Exercises and Cardio. Sessions keeps the existing calendar, day details, machine filters and workout cards, with the latest three weeks shown first and Show more for older workouts.

Exercises has a bounded, searchable library with a live progress preview below on phones and beside it on wider screens. Date-range buttons sit beside the preview value. Open full progress for records and session history, then return with your search, list position and range intact. Older History, Progress and Cardio links still work.

Follows are now friendships. Send a friend request, and once it is accepted you both see each other’s shared training. Requests always need accepting, even for public profiles. Existing follows in either direction became friendships, and waiting follow requests became friend requests.

Social has its own bottom tab. Friends shows each friend once with their latest session, a seven-day activity strip and a reaction button. Find holds friend requests, people search, requests you sent and blocked members. Remove or block a friend from their profile. Home keeps its compact friends card.

Your profile now uses the same training layout as other members, with your calendar, training totals and workouts. Edit your name and photo here. Sharing, account ID, password, sign-out and account deletion are now in Settings. Private profiles can preview their own page without enabling sharing, without a private-profile reminder in the header.
Time trained and Profile sharing keep their explanations behind question-mark help buttons. The collapsed What you share arrow points down, independently of its parent section.
Progress changes are green for increases, red for decreases, and neutral when unchanged across estimated 1RM, top set and volume.

Training’s Sessions view starts with the latest workout week and the two preceding calendar weeks, using your week-start preference. Show more reveals older workouts, and links to older sessions still open them directly.
Quick-start circles are now 52 px across, up from 44 px, with larger icons to make each option easier to see and tap.
Swipe down from the muscle details handle or header to close the sheet. You can also pull down on its content when the list is at the top; short pulls return to place and scrolling still works.
Removed the redundant Contributing exercises heading and count from muscle details. Done, Escape and tapping outside still close the sheet.

Remove an individual rest by choosing 0:00 (no rest) or swiping left on its row. Undo restores it; removed rests remain removed when editing, saving or reopening the workout. Rest choices include 0:30. Show rest times in Settings hides the rows independently of the automatic rest timer.

highlights.title: Settings, with a place for everything
highlights.description: Browse six focused sections with saved-value summaries. Search opens the right panel and control; unfinished edits stay with you as you move between sections. Training defaults, appearance, alerts, account privacy and data tools each have a clear home.

image.alt: The redesigned Settings overview with six focused categories, search and synthetic account preferences.

highlights.title: Keep moving while saves finish
highlights.description: Finish a workout or save an old session, then keep browsing. Saving indicators, completion PRs and routine notices leave navigation and scrolling available. Failed saves keep your entries for retry.

image.alt: Finish a synthetic workout, navigate during its save, then open Body while the completion PR notice remains visible.

highlights.title: Your training stays in sync
highlights.description: Saved training changes from your other devices appear automatically. The visible app checks every five seconds and when you return or reconnect, while keeping your active workout and unsaved entries.

image.alt: A workout saved in a separate signed-in sample session appears on the desktop without reloading the page.

highlights.title: Your profile, focused on training
highlights.description: View your calendar, training totals and workouts in the same layout as your friends. Edit your name and photo here; manage privacy, your account and security in Settings. Your own page stays available when your profile is private.

image.alt: An isolated sample member's own profile with name and photo editing, workout totals and the consistency calendar, while their profile remains private.

highlights.title: Your training, together
highlights.description: Sessions keeps the calendar and saved workouts. Exercises opens familiar progress tools, and Cardio stays within reach. Switch tabs and return to the view you were using.

image.alt: Training Sessions retains the calendar above the latest three weeks of workouts.

highlights.title: Library + preview
highlights.description: Scroll the exercise library without losing your place. Select a lift to update its preview and use 1M, 3M, 9M or 1Y beside the value. Open full progress for records and saved sessions.

image.alt: A bounded exercise library above its live progress preview on a phone, with range controls beside the value and synthetic training data.

highlights.title: Friends, not followers
highlights.description: Send one friend request; once it is accepted you both see each other. Friends lists everyone once with their latest session and week. Find holds requests and people search.

image.alt: Social Friends tab listing synthetic friends once each, with a seven-day activity strip, latest session and reaction button.

highlights.title: Your account, on every tab
highlights.description: Open Notifications or Profile beside Settings on Home, Training, Social and Body. Matching buttons keep the same order and wrap neatly on smaller screens.

image.alt: Body with matching Notifications, Profile and Settings buttons at the top right and no duplicate header plus, using synthetic account data.

highlights.title: Progress at a glance
highlights.description: Green means an increase and red means a decrease. Unchanged values stay neutral across estimated 1RM, top set and volume.

image.alt: Training Exercises uses the existing Pec Deck chart, records and red decrease comparison with synthetic data.

highlights.title: Larger quick-start circles
highlights.description: The bottom quick-start menu has slightly larger circles and icons for Cardio, Up next and Empty.

image.alt: Quick-start menu with larger Cardio, Up next and Empty circles.

highlights.title: Pull down to close muscle details
highlights.description: The sheet follows your finger. Short pulls return to place, and a deliberate downward swipe closes it. Exercise details sit directly below the goal.

image.alt: A short downward pull returns muscle details to place; a longer pull dismisses the sheet, with exercises listed without a redundant heading.

highlights.title: Remove a rest, keep the set
highlights.description: Choose 0:00 (no rest) or swipe left on a rest row. Undo restores it. Removed rests stay removed when editing, saving or reopening; edit the set to add one back. Show rest times in Settings hides rows independently of the countdown.

image.alt: An isolated sample workout removes a rest with zero time, restores it with Undo, then removes it with a left swipe while retaining both sets.
